hero.title: Agile, Scrum and Jira: deliver value in small steps
hero.subtitle: Write user stories, prioritise a backlog, forecast with velocity and track a burndown, all in working spreadsheet and document labs. Every task is checked and explained.

Pass each module quiz (70% or more). You can retry as often as you like.
Complete the sprint plan and the final assessment.

faq.q: Do I need to use Jira?
faq.a: No. The labs run in your browser. The course explains the concepts common to Jira and similar trackers so you can use any tool.

faq.q: Is this a Scrum certification course?
faq.a: No. It teaches the framework and practices, but it is not an official certification preparation and does not award a certification from any external body.
No. Agile is used in marketing, product, education and operations too.

activities.title: Write user stories with acceptance criteria
activities.objective: Write stories in the 'As a, I want, so that' form with clear acceptance criteria.
activities.scenario: A college app lets students see library availability. Write three user stories for it.
steps: Write three stories, each as a Heading 2 with a short title.
Under each, write a paragraph: 'As a ..., I want ..., so that ...'.
Under each, add a bulleted list of at least two acceptance criteria (testable statements).
Keep it between 120 and 320 words.

checks.label: Three story titles
checks.hint: Use Heading 2 for each title.
checks.explain: A short title helps the backlog stay readable.

checks.label: The 'As a' form
checks.hint: Start each story with 'As a'.
checks.explain: It names who the story is for.

checks.label: I want
checks.hint: Include 'I want'.

checks.label: So that
checks.hint: Include 'so that'.

checks.label: Acceptance criteria lists
checks.hint: Use bullets of at least two items.
checks.explain: Acceptance criteria make a story testable.

checks.label: Testable wording
checks.hint: Use words like should, can, shows or when.

spec.what: testable words such as shows or should

checks.label: Between 120 and 320 words
checks.hint: Concise.

activities.title: Prioritise a backlog by value
activities.objective: Rank backlog items by value for effort and decide what fits in a sprint.
activities.scenario: A product owner has six items scored for value and effort. Rank them by value per point and pick items that fit a 20-point sprint.
steps: In D2 work out value per point: value divided by effort. Fill down.
In B9 total the effort of the three items chosen in column E (mark 1 for chosen).
Mark 1 in E for the three items with the highest value per point.
In B10 total their value with SUMIF on column E.
In B11 show OK if the chosen effort fits the capacity in B8.

checks.label: D2 is value per point
D7 is filled
checks.hint: Fill down.

checks.label: B9 totals the chosen effort
checks.hint: =SUMIF(E2:E7,1,C2:C7)
checks.explain: Add efforts where the item is chosen.

checks.label: B10 totals the chosen value
checks.hint: =SUMIF(E2:E7,1,B2:B7)
checks.explain: Add values where the item is chosen.

checks.label: B11 checks capacity
checks.hint: =IF(B9<=B8,"OK","Too much")
checks.explain: The sprint should not exceed its capacity.

activities.title: Forecast with velocity
activities.objective: Calculate average velocity and forecast how many sprints a backlog needs.
activities.scenario: The team completed story points in its last five sprints. Forecast how long the remaining 120 points will take.
steps: In B8 find the average velocity with AVERAGE.
In B9 find the lowest and in B10 the highest sprint with MIN and MAX.
In B11 forecast sprints at average velocity: remaining points divided by average (round up with ROUNDUP to 0 digits).
In B12 forecast sprints at the lowest velocity (worst case).
In B13 forecast sprints at the highest velocity (best case).

checks.label: B8 is the average velocity
checks.hint: =AVERAGE(B2:B6)
checks.explain: The mean of the five sprints.

checks.label: B9 is the lowest sprint
checks.hint: =MIN(B2:B6)

checks.label: B10 is the highest sprint
checks.hint: =MAX(B2:B6)

checks.label: B11 is the sprints needed at average
checks.hint: =ROUNDUP(B7/B8,0)
checks.explain: Round up: a part sprint still needs a sprint.

checks.label: B12 is the worst case
checks.hint: =ROUNDUP(B7/B9,0)

checks.label: B13 is the best case
checks.hint: =ROUNDUP(B7/B10,0)

activities.title: Run a retrospective
activities.objective: Write retrospective notes with what went well, what to improve and specific actions.
activities.scenario: Your team finished a sprint where two stories slipped to the next sprint. Write the retro notes.
steps: Add Heading 2 sections: Went well, To improve, Actions.
Write at least two bullets under Went well and two under To improve.
Under Actions write a numbered list of at least two actions, each with an owner and a due date or sprint.
Keep it between 80 and 220 words.

checks.hint: Use Heading 2.
checks.explain: A simple three-part format works well.

checks.label: In order
checks.hint: Went well, To improve, Actions.

checks.label: Bulleted lists of observations
checks.hint: Use bullets.
checks.explain: Short observations are easy to discuss.

checks.hint: Use the numbered list button.

activities.title: Track a sprint burndown
activities.objective: Calculate remaining work each day and compare it with the ideal line.
activities.scenario: A sprint began with 40 points. Daily completed points are recorded. Work out remaining points and compare with the ideal burndown.
steps: In C2 enter remaining points after day 1: starting points minus points done on day 1 (B2).
In C3 enter =C2-B3 and fill down to C6.
In D2 enter the ideal remaining: starting points minus (starting points / 5) times the day number; fill down.
In E2 show Ahead, On track or Behind compared with the ideal.
Chart the remaining points as a line.

checks.label: C2 is remaining after day 1
C6 reaches zero
D2 is the ideal after day 1
D6 is the ideal on day 5
checks.hint: Fill down.

checks.label: E2 compares actual and ideal
checks.hint: =IF(C2<D2,"Ahead",IF(C2=D2,"On track","Behind"))
checks.explain: Less remaining than ideal is ahead.

checks.label: A line chart of remaining points
checks.hint: Chart type line with labels A2:A6 and values C2:C6.
checks.explain: A burndown chart shows trend at a glance.

activities.title: Final project: plan a sprint
activities.objective: Write a sprint plan with a goal, selected stories, capacity, risks and a definition of done.
activities.scenario: Plan the first two-week sprint of the library app project for a team of four with a capacity of 24 points.
steps: Add a Heading 1 'Sprint 1 plan'.
Add Heading 2 sections: Sprint goal, Selected stories, Capacity, Definition of done, Risks.
Under Selected stories write a bulleted list of at least four stories with points.
Under Definition of done list at least three criteria.
Under Capacity show the total points against the capacity of 24.
Keep it between 140 and 330 words.

checks.label: A title
checks.hint: Use Heading 1.

checks.label: Five sections
checks.hint: Use Heading 2.
checks.explain: A sprint plan has standard parts.

checks.label: Sections in order
checks.hint: Sprint goal, Selected stories, Capacity, Definition of done, Risks.
checks.explain: From purpose to work to checks.

checks.label: A one-sentence goal
checks.hint: Write a single clear sentence.
checks.explain: A goal gives the sprint a purpose.

checks.label: At least four stories
checks.hint: Use the bullet button.
checks.explain: Choose enough to fill the capacity.

checks.label: Points appear
checks.hint: Include numbers followed by points.

checks.label: Capacity of 24 is mentioned
checks.hint: Mention 24.

checks.label: Between 140 and 330 words
checks.hint: One page.
